nodes.description: Under normal experimental conditions, AMBRA1 acts as a mitochondrial scaffold for RMC1, and RMC1 directly interacts with HUWE1 to recruit it to mitochondria. Disease-associated noncatalytic variants disrupt this recruitment, so the abnormal state modeled here is failed mitochondrial targeting rather than normal recruitment. This compartment-specific route is not generalized to all HUWE1 substrates or alleles.

evidence.reference_title: HUWE1 targets mitochondria via RMC1 to promote neurodevelopment.
evidence.snippet: Mechanistically, AMBRA1 acts as a mitochondrial scaffold that recruits RMC1, enabling HUWE1 localization to mitochondria through direct interaction with RMC1.

nodes.description: HUWE1 is a HECT-domain E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase implicated in regulation of the neuronal cell cycle. Xp11.22 duplications can increase HUWE1 expression, while different missense alleles can decrease or increase HUWE1 protein and shift the abundance of its substrates p53 and Mcl-1 in opposite directions. The direct evidence therefore supports allele-specific dysregulation of HUWE1-dependent substrate homeostasis, not a uniform loss or gain of catalytic activity across the allelic spectrum. This abundance/substrate branch is kept distinct from the AMBRA1-RMC1 mitochondrial-recruitment branch because the available evidence does not establish a causal connection between them.

nodes.description: In Juberg-Marsidi syndrome cells, p.G4310R reduces HUWE1 stability and protein abundance. The mutant HECT domain ubiquitinates p53 with efficiency similar to wild type, so this node represents an allele-specific stability defect rather than impaired catalytic p53 ubiquitination. It must not be generalized to all HUWE1 sequence variants or to regional Xp11.22 copy gains.
